chunks: From him, from his father, from Fadl al-Nawfali, from Abu Yahya al-Razi, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Do not mix with or do business with anyone except one who grew up in goodness."

key_terms.نَشَأَ فِي الْخَيْرِ: grew up in goodness / was raised in virtue

ai.seo_question: Who should Muslims choose to associate with and do business with according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In the context of commercial ethics within *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes that moral upbringing is a prerequisite for trustworthy trade, linking personal piety to economic reliability. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly view that *mu'amalat* (transactions) are not merely legal contracts but spiritual engagements, where associating with the virtuous (*al-khayr*) safeguards against the corruption of *riba* and ensures the purity of wealth.
